verification_methodology_note: Allegiance Commission Law «نظام هيئة البيعة» — Royal Order A/135, dated 26/9/1427H (NOT 18/10/1427H as sometimes cited elsewhere -- 18/10 is the Gregorian day/month, 18 October 2006, misattributed as a Hijri date in some secondary references; all three independent Arabic full-text sources used here agree on 26/9/1427H as the Hijri date). Issued by King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. Flat structure, 25 articles, no chapters. The BOE legal portal's exact LawDetails page for this law was located (GUID 3213c2f6-eaf8-45dc-8f8c-a9a700f167ee) but was UNREACHABLE by every method tried this research pass: direct WebFetch returned HTTP 503; the r.jina.ai reader-proxy (both WebFetch and raw curl, with retries) returned HTTP 422 / TimeoutError, indicating BOE's own SPA could not be crawled by the proxy's headless browser; and the Wayback Machine, despite a valid archived snapshot existing (confirmed via its own availability API), was blocked by this sandbox's network egress policy. No claim in this track is BOE-primary-verified. Instead, THREE INDEPENDENT ARABIC SECONDARY SOURCES were fetched and cross-compared directly (not just search snippets): ar.wikisource.org (raw MediaWiki wikitext), islamport.com/الموسوعة الشاملة (raw HTML, windows-1256 encoding detected and corrected), and ar.wikipedia.org's 'هيئة البيعة السعودية' article (raw wikitext, includes a full reproduction of all 25 articles). These three sources agree on all 25 articles almost word-for-word, with only non-substantive orthographic variants (hamza placement, spelling conventions) in islamport.com's text. This is a strong same-language (Arabic-to-Arabic) triple-source convergence, though still not a BOE-primary verification -- flagged as 'secondary-source verified, primary-source pending' pending a future BOE retry from a different network path. The Royal Order's own preamble contains a self-amending clause: clause 'ثانيا' of the promulgation order amends Article 5, paragraph (c), of the Basic Law of Governance (Royal Order A/90, 27/8/1412H) to read: '(ج - تتم الدعوة لمبايعة الملك، واختيار ولي العهد وفقا لنظام هيئة البيعة)' -- this CONTRADICTS the wording currently shown in this corpus's own Basic Law of Governance track (Article 5c: 'يختار الملك ولي العهد، ويعفيه بأمر ملكي'), which was extracted from the BOE portal and WIPO Lex earlier this session. This is a genuine, significant, UNRESOLVED discrepancy between two tracks in this corpus, flagged here rather than silently reconciled in either direction -- see known_unresolved_discrepancies for the full detail; a dedicated verification pass has been dispatched separately to determine the CURRENT in-force wording of Basic Law of Governance Article 5(c) before either track is altered. Clause 'ثالثا' of the same promulgation order states this law's provisions apply only PROSPECTIVELY, not to the then-reigning King (Abdullah) or then-Crown-Prince (Sultan). No amendment to this law's own 25-article text was found in any source since 2006; a companion Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام هيئة البيعة) was issued separately by Royal Order A/164 (26/9/1428H) but its full text was not extracted in this pass and is not part of this track.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: Article 21's final clause reads 'وما يتصل بتأجيل الاجتماع، أو وقفه' (matters relating to the POSTPONEMENT of the meeting, or its suspension) per two of three independent sources (ar.wikisource.org, ar.wikipedia.org). islamport.com's independent transcription instead has 'وما يتصل بتعديل الاجتماع أو وقفه' (matters relating to the AMENDMENT/modification of the meeting, or its suspension). The majority reading ('تأجيل'/postponement) is used in this track's ingested text, on the basis of 2-of-3 source agreement plus better contextual coherence (postponement/suspension is a natural pairing; amendment/suspension is an odd one) -- but this was NOT confirmed against the BOE primary source, so the minority reading is preserved here rather than silently discarded.

This law's own Royal Order A/135 promulgation preamble (clause 'ثانيا') claims to amend Article 5, paragraph (c), of the Basic Law of Governance (Royal Order A/90) to read: '(ج - تتم الدعوة لمبايعة الملك، واختيار ولي العهد وفقا لنظام هيئة البيعة)'. This DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the wording currently ingested in this corpus's own Basic Law of Governance track (Article 5c: 'يختار الملك ولي العهد، ويعفيه بأمر ملكي'), which was extracted from the BOE portal and cross-checked against WIPO Lex earlier this session. Possible explanations include: the BOE/WIPO Lex source used for the Basic Law of Governance track reflects an outdated pre-2006 snapshot; the 2006 amendment was itself later reverted or superseded; or a transcription issue in one of the sources. This is a GENUINE, SIGNIFICANT, UNRESOLVED cross-track discrepancy -- NOT silently resolved in either direction. A dedicated verification pass has been separately dispatched to determine the current in-force text before any correction is made to either track.

The BOE portal's exact LawDetails page for this law was located (GUID 3213c2f6-eaf8-45dc-8f8c-a9a700f167ee) but was unreachable by every method tried this research pass (direct fetch 503, r.jina.ai proxy 422/timeout, Wayback Machine blocked by sandbox egress policy despite a valid archived snapshot existing). This track rests on triple independent Arabic secondary-source cross-verification (ar.wikisource.org, islamport.com, ar.wikipedia.org) rather than the BOE primary source used for most other tracks in this corpus. A fresh BOE retry from a different network path is recommended before this track is treated as fully primary-source-anchored.
